page.sub: A customer's design goes in; a finished, boxed lamp comes out. Laser cutting and engraving, assembly, inspection, packing and coding on one conveyor loop, fed by an automated warehouse and a mobile robot.
page.description: The Night Lamp production line at Phoenix Industrial Labs: a personalized night lamp made to order by students. Laser cutting and engraving, assembly, vision inspection, packing and coding on one conveyor loop, fed by an automated warehouse and a mobile robot.
page.image_alt: Night lamp production line: automated warehouse and mobile robot at the left, laser, assembly and inspection stations along a conveyor loop, packing and coding at the right
page.image2_alt: The night lamp line seen from the other side: fenced robot cells, enclosed laser stations, the control cabinet and the conveyor loop
facts: process stations on one conveyor loop

route.p: Nine stops from a customer's design to a boxed lamp back on the shelf.
steps: A customer's design and text arrive at the control and display center, which schedules the job and follows it around the loop.
The automated warehouse holds blanks and finished lamps on smart pallets. It picks a blank, and the mobile robot carries the pallet to the conveyor loop.
A laser cuts the lamp panel to shape and engraves the customer's design into it.
Laser marking adds the order code, so every lamp can be traced back to the order that made it.
At the assembly station the engraved panel meets its holder and becomes a lamp.
An in-line vision system checks the engraving and the assembly before anything is packed.
The lamp is boxed at the packaging station.
An inkjet prints the order code on the box, and a scanner reads it back to close the loop on traceability.
The finished order rides the mobile robot back to the warehouse, ready for pickup, and the job closes on the display center.

items: The lasers, robots, controllers, vision systems and sensors are industrial products, so the line can take on outside production work as well as teaching.
Every station stands on casters with leveling feet. Use one on its own for a lesson, or join them all into the full line.
The whole line exists in simulation. Students assemble and commission it virtually first, then move to the real machines.
Storage and logistics, the production area, a digital-twin teaching area, and the control and display center.

skills.p: Mechanical, electrical, pneumatic and hydraulic, robotics and controls work, grouped by what a technician actually touches.
groups: PLC programming, HMI screens, fieldbus and industrial networking, sensors and detection.
Servo and motor control, speed regulation, pneumatics and hydraulics.
Robot programming and teaching, simulation and commissioning, vision and sensing, and typical robot applications.
The automated warehouse and the mobile robot: operation, communication, path planning, and RFID tracking.
Laser marking, CNC principles and programming, CAD/CAM.
Installing, wiring and maintaining an automated line, integrated wiring, and computer networks.
skills.more: This is the floor where semesters three to five happen.
